tips.comment: Well backed on his return to turf at Brighton, a close-up 4th despite not being able to get a clear run at a key time. Clearly well enough treated from the same mark to get his head in front if things drop kinder for him this time from 3 lb below his sole winning mark.
Calafrio only missed out by a neck a few weeks ago on the return. I would expect more now, second up, with her only win to date being on GF.
Dropped in class and off a very handy mark. Should go close based on past runs here. First run back after that long break was probably just a prep run.

Races mainly on the AW but last raced here in October after a break and got a good 4th, only a length and a half off the leader. Is now 7lb lower than that today, so looks very well treated by the handicapper.
Still a maiden after 19 runs, but has put up some encouraging runs this year and is running off a mark where, at the very least, he can be competitive, especially if improvements are made.
CITY OF STRANGERS missed out over the five furlongs yesterday but was hugely effective when last seen over six furlongs and could well defy the weight rise for that win returning to this distance.

Monticristo Bay is a pretty consistent individual who has found a good opportunity here as this class 6 handicap is not as competitive as it may seem at a quick glance of the form book and it should also suit him well was last seen at Southwell 25 days ago where finishing a very respectable 3rd/8 that was his return run after a 139 day break and it was full of promise entitled to strip fitter with that run under his belt he should also be a lot sharper at the finish this time out steps back up in trip going over the 6 furlong trip here that being a good move by his connections currently operating on an unchanged mark of 57 N Tinkler's inmate looks poised to strike here and can do even better now as a 3yo jockey Faye Mcmanoman takes the ride that being a positive booking as this jockey knows the horse well and has steered him to a fine win in the past must be considered in a race of this nature

Olympic Melody lines up today at Nottingham after a quiet return at Chelmsford, where she was well backed but finished fifth, 7 lengths behind the winner. That was her first run for a new yard and her handicap debut, so she’s entitled to come on for it. Now racing off 56 in a modest Class 6, she could take a step forward with that run under her belt.
Firmly at the bottom of the handicap mark with a 5lb claimer. Although handicaps have not gone to plan on AW, I hope the switch to turf at handicap level and the dropped mark has a positive impact.

Finished 4th of 9 in a Class 2 Novice Stakes at Kempton last September and was well beaten the next twice. Makes stable debut for a new yard here on seasonal return at Class 6 level and could go well at decent odds.

Expressionless had two good wins last summer, with the latest of those being a C3 on GF off a 73. He returned from a break last month to a decent C4 third off a 73 on GD. I would expect more now, second up off the same mark but on GF.
Both career wins have come on good to firm going, which is forecast today. One of those wins was over today's trip. The jockey is in good form with 5 wins in the last 7 days.

Damascus Steel is a lot more interesting than the form book on paper is suggesting here was last seen at Kempton 14 days ago where finishing 8th/12 however he did shape better than that bare result suggests and he was returning from a 102 day break on the occasion and is most certainly entitled to strip fitter with that run under his belt and will be a lot sharper at the finish this time out steps back up in trip that being a good move by his connections and the combination of a suitable distance his ideal pace level at his disposal and a suitable turf track that will be play well into his strengths makes Ed Dunlop's inmate a serious contender here currently operating on a mark of 73 Damascus Steel looks poised to strike and ticks all boxes to do so and worth noting he is now operating 2lb below his last winning mark and he must be taken seriously and accordingly here . Respected . I also have a selection with this jockey / trainer combination in race 6 here at Nottingham and is worth a look into best of luck to all following and good day to all
This ARmateur Derby winner showed ability on return from layoff last time and has dropped dangerously in the weights, which can spark a surprise effort.

The model I run suggests Con Te Partiro can cause an upset here. Odds are huge, so each way still offers value. Sets out with the second highest RPR of the field, has the joint lowest rating, and therefore the lowest weight to carry over the reasonably long 1m6f trip.
Had a shocker LTO when 16 of 16 at Lingfield this month, but has won off a much higher mark in the past and has the ability to bounce back strongly off this mark tomorrow.

The model I run suggests Noisy Jazz should win this race. The race simulation has Noisy Jazz in first, Under the Twilight in second, and Bellarchi in third. This result has largely been driven by Noisy Jazz having the highest RPR and drops in class today from the previous two races.
Trainer's only runner here today. He has two at nearby Southwell tomorrow. She has to have a chance based on her last mark now being well below her Ascot win last spring.

Ended last season being placed in Group company before winning a Listed race at Goodwood and ended the season with a very respectable 4th at odds of 40/1 in Group company at Newmarket. Ground and trip are ideal today and if fit enough will be very difficult to beat.
Has been placed a couple of times at this level. Ran well at Kempton last month and could go in today's for in-form jockey.
Best form came on good to firm ground when runner-up twice at listed level. Has run well fresh before, and this is not a strong field. Main player if ready to fire.
Hasn't been seen since November when getting off the mark at the second attempt with an easy win at Southwell. Should make the frame today for an in-form yard that has a good record at the track.

Daughter of Oasis Dream who makes her seasonal reappearance here after a 225 day break and strongly appeals as the type do much better now as a 3yo and should be a lot more street wise as 3yo currently operating on a mark of 61 it is very well possible that Ed Dunlop's inmate is a good step ahead of the accesor at this stage given the way his career has developed and should be much better than a mark 61 as a 3yo arrives here in top nick as he is good hands back home and can be whole different proposition this season jockey Rossa Ryan takes the ride and can give Crocodile River a promising return run here at Nottingham

Beach Point heads to Nottingham today after a strong second at Yarmouth on seasonal return. That run confirmed he’s still improving, and with Oisin Murphy booked and only a 1lb rise, he looks ready to go one better. ￼
Was sent off as favorite over course and distance 17 days ago when runner-up to a decent-looking performer that day. Could make amends today for an in-form trainer.
Placed at Beverley 12 days ago, 6/19 at Doncaster just before that, and runs off the same mark again today. That kind of form should see him pushing near the front today.
Definitely worth a go at such a big price. Loves this trip and is on a very low mark. Will need to get a nice early position from the widest draw.

Flatley returned from a short break last month to a C6 win and went up to a 64 but could not follow up with both runs being on the AW. I think the return to GF turf, a surface he won on last July when running off a 67, could bring him back in the game EW.

Beaten favorite here last time 17 days ago when running out of puff in the final furlong. Drop back in trip will suit, as will change of jockey who won 3 times on this horse last year, all over today's course and distance.

Apart from the obvious Shaw Park going well. I'm going to take a chance on the now 11 year old Poetic Force here at Brighton. He has decent course form and will saddle 8st 8lbs (with Molly Gunn's allowance) on his back tomorrow. He had 9st on his back (Molly Gunn took off 7lbs) when he was 2nd at Brighton on 8th Oct last year, and if he brings that turf form back to Brighton, he should hopefully go well. Good course trainer. Molly Gunn rides again in this apprentice handicap. Lots of positives.

This looks like a good chance for Tawasol to open his account. After a good 2nd at Wolverhampton, where he was a little unlucky suffering interference, he stayed on well. Returned from absence last time out back on turf to finish 2nd. Will be better for that outing and should be able to get his head in front today.

El Madar has been slowly getting a bit nearer the front with each of the four runs so far, with the latest being in C2. Interestingly, he returns from the break today after wind surgery, which is when I would normally expect to see some improvement while stepping back to C5.

Best run for a mark was the only time that she ran on turf at Goodwood so she has experience with a switchback track. That will be a big help for her here, representing a yard that has a solid record at this track. She travelled really well that day and is interesting here on her handicap debut.
He enjoys sharper tracks with good runs over hurdles and on the flat on them, including a win at Sligo. He is just 1lb higher today. He has a great chance based on his form over hurdles.

GALILEO'S COMPASS has had to change trainers twice due to poor performance, but has consequently moved down the weights. More improvement could have been made during the long absence since last seen in action in August 2024.
Progressive last season but shaped as if there was much more to come. Yard has only sent nine runners to Brighton in the last five seasons and has won with five of them.

On her seasonal reappearance, Lady Ridgewood split a Dubawi filly and a Frankel filly from the Balding and Gosden yards at Newbury. Gosden's Queen of Thieves won next time out by 11 lengths. That might suggest that Lady Ridgewood should be rated a lot higher than 79 for her handicap debut. She can front run, so the track and small field may not be an issue.

Won at this course, finished 3rd here at today's distance and course in a very quick time at a mark of 83 in a class 3 event. Sire 'Zarak' shows an overall 50% win rate at this course, on a very small number of runs here. Recent 3rd at Windsor course and distance in a quick-timed event, just 1lb above today's mark. And with a 7lb claimer jockey on board and the fact the horse ran well here in a class 3 event, today's odds look generous against the favorite, who is yet to run on turf.

Did better on his handicap debut than he had in three runs for a mark. He is a half-sibling to a couple of smart types, including a Group 2 winner, so no surprise if he improves for both his first run on the turf and for the general experience.

Emily Rebecca stepped up in trip to 1m2f in February and was second, just over a length away from the winner on handicap debut. She could go well again off the same mark but with handy Alec Voikhansky claiming 3 lbs, if getting on with the change to turf.
Showed promise Lto when 6th at Lingfield on the AW. That was over 1m and now upped to 1m 2f for handicap debut. Fairly open race here and decent odds. Should be able to make the frame at least.

Three places paid in this 9-runner race, and this outsider might be the surprise package on debut for a new stable, taking a big step up in trip. That extra trip should certainly suit on breeding, and this is only the horse's 5th race, so it's far too soon to give up on her yet. She is in just her 2nd handicap here, and the trainer tends to only book his excellent 3lb claiming apprentice when he thinks he has a well-handicapped horse on his hands. The jockey also has a record at this course, which is way better than most jockeys (10 wins from just 52 rides), and the trainer has a good course record too.

He won over 7f here last year and is just 3lbs higher today. He was just a neck behind the re-opposing Comedian Leader and is 1lb better off, so should be able to turn the tables. They were 4 lengths clear of the 3rd and have a great chance.

She won over course and distance last year in a classified race and despite this being her first turf run in almost a year, she is now 4lbs lower than her Salisbury 2nd on her last turf start. She has since won on the all weather off a 2lbs higher mark and finally returns to the surface where she has a more prolific record.

Brighton regular and 3-time course winner HEER'S SADIE won on her second start last season and she caught my eye running-on on her seasonal debut over C&D 17-days ago after being dropped in from a poor draw in stall 1. She then had to come 9-wide on the home straight before finishing a decent 6.25 lengths 5th of 9 in a slightly higher Grade (0-55 as opposed to this 0-52 race). She should strip fitter for the run, she is unexposed at this 1-mile trip (and may even need this distance now a 7 year old mare), and better drawn in stall 6 she looks worth an each way interest at the 16/1 with Bet365 who are paying the first 4 home in this 14-runner race.

A very poor-looking handicap where Cherry Hill appeals at a big-looking 20/1. With 4 places up for grabs, he looks excellent each-way value. He will be fitter for a recent run and was running well off higher marks on the all-weather last back end.
Shop Local makes her yard debut today at Brighton off a basement mark of 46. She showed little last season but drops into a weak race and could take a big step forward.
Won nicely 8 days ago over today's distance and on good to firm going. Trainer has a good record at the track and apprentice takes off a useful 7 lbs.

His peak RPR this year and last year have both come on his only Brighton start when placing on both occasions. He is 4 lbs lower than his 2nd last year, and he is on the same mark as his 3rd over course and distance last time out when beaten less than a length, so he should be able to run well kept to this track.

The 4yo is a previous 6f C/D winner. He ran a nice race over this C/D two weeks ago for a new yard, after coming off a 3 month break, front ranked and holding every chance inside the final furlong, outpaced late on. Something to build on, a 3lb lower mark now and he was rated 15lb higher last summer.

Just one win from 21 runs is not the kind of return I am looking for. And now 18 runs since that win last year, but keeps dropping down the weights. So it would not surprise me if he puts up a solid performance off the current mark.
Even money favourite when finishing runner up at Bath 11 days ago. The winner that day has franked the form by winning next time out so should make amends here.

Weakened inside the final furlong over a mile and a half at Lingfield last time out. Will welcome the return to the extended mile here, being beaten a neck over course and distance in the race prior to that.

Simon & Ed Crisford's trained filly displayed plenty of greenness when only beaten a neck into 2nd over 1m at Newcastle on her debut earlier this month. The daughter of Frankel clearly has plenty of ability, so could be hard to beat.

The Cutest makes her handicap debut at Wolverhampton after showing promise as a juvenile. Dropping to 5f might sharpen her up and with a good draw and Luke Morris booked, she looks ready to get involved.

Pysanka has immediately caught my attention here and anyone following will likely know why as i selected him to win 8 days ago over this course and distance and he won at a handsome price of 12/1 proving my statement that this is no horse to overlook over this course and distance and has found another excellent opportunity just 8 days on carries a penalty here for that success however that is of no concern and he has been very competitive of this sort of mark before that being a mark of 63 D M Loughnane's inmate is likely to give this a very good shot and he also looks to be the fitest in the line up and can put that to good effect here in a race that shouldn't take much winning jockey Edward Greatrex takes the ride an can steer Pysanka to another success here

Baileys Jubilation returns to Wolverhampton today after a couple of modest runs at Lingfield. She previously went close over 6f here, finishing a narrow second off a similar mark. Back down to 5f in a small field, she could be dangerous if allowed to dictate the pace.

Shaped really well on reappearance when finishing a nose 2nd. The winner finished a very close 3rd next time out from a mark of 71 and Radio Star can get her nose in front if improving for that effort.
STARTLING won here over C&D on last visit, and poor performance has reduced the weight dangerously close to the last winning mark. So, this return could revive fortunes with some luck.

Barney’s Bay lines up today at Wolverhampton following a solid fourth at Southwell over 7f, where he stayed on well late. He’s now 2lb below his last winning mark and has a decent record on the all-weather. With a strong pace likely, he could be finishing best of all.

Just four career runs for the 4yo filly and room for more improvement. Beaten just over a length on her handicap debut, at this track, seeing the race out nicely. She’s had a nice 3 month break, she has a 2lb lower mark now and the extra furlong could help.
No wins from 13 runs to date and no impact yet for new yard when a shocking 12 of 12 LTO at Bath earlier this month. But hoping now operating at the lowest career mark kickstarts his handicap career.
